audit_findings.title: Parent-share denominator may be paired with partly consolidated owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.357m FY2025 NCI income and $32.501m latest NCI equity; exact OE mismatch unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable net income is combined with potentially unadjusted consolidated depreciation, working capital, capital expenditures and bridge cash before division by 74.988m parent shares.
audit_findings.evidence: The interests of non-controlling shareholders in these consolidated entities are presented as net income attributable to noncontrolling interest in the Consolidated Statements of Operations and as noncontrolling interest in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that noncontrolling interests exist, but the supplied record does not establish whether the OE reconstruction ownership-adjusted every consolidated component. Cash and add-backs attributable to NCI would overstate parent value, while ownership-adjusting capital expenditures and working capital could move OE either way. The net effect cannot be established from the supplied totals.
audit_findings.action: Prepare an entity-by-entity ownership schedule for FY2025 and June 2026, rebuild OE using only the parent economic share of every add-back, working-capital movement and capital expenditure, adjust bridge cash for NCI ownership, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A $38.819 million acquisition-related expense may distort the anchor despite not representing additional cash
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the nonrecurring acquisition-related compensation charge reduces FY2025 net income and therefore the OE anchor; if already reversed through cash-flow classification, another add-back would double count it.
audit_findings.evidence: These amounts do not represent additional cash paid at closing, but rather a recharacterization of a portion of the total proceeds.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the charge was recognized in operating expense and represented a reallocation of purchase proceeds rather than additional acquisition cash. It does not demonstrate how the $105.4m OE calculation treated the charge. Its size relative to the anchor is sufficient to materially alter the valuation outputs, so this is an unresolved material treatment issue rather than a demonstrated anchor error.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $38.819m from net income through the operating-cash-flow reconciliation and acquisition cash outflow, identify its tax effect, then rerun the valuation with exactly one normalization if—and only if—it remains in OE.

audit_findings.title: Cash-settled TIP awards are a potential senior cash claim, not merely a no-dilution item
audit_findings.magnitude: filed grant-date fair value of $10.590m for each class; aggregate expected and maximum cash payouts unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Achievement of the EBITA conditions would create compensation expense and a cash liability that reduces forecast OE or must be deducted from the equity bridge; it does not increase common shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon achievement, the Growth Shares will be settled in cash, and thus, are liability-classified and will be remeasured at fair value at each reporting date until settlement.
audit_findings.explanation: The TIP is a forward-looking contingent claim. No expense or liability had been recognized through June 2026 because achievement was not considered probable, so there is no demonstrated omission from current reported numbers. Nevertheless, growth supporting the valuation scenarios could also trigger payouts, making this a scenario-dependent claim requiring monitoring.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the TIP award agreement and payout tables, calculate expected and maximum cash settlements under bear, base and bull EBITA paths, and include each payout exactly once in forecast OE or the equity bridge when probability becomes supportable.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration appears omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.265m latest filed liability, equal to approximately $0.20 per share and 0.8%-1.3% of scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: The acquisition-related cash claim ranks ahead of common equity and should either reduce the equity bridge or be captured through forecast OE cash payments.
audit_findings.evidence: The maximum consideration which can be paid over the consideration period of five years is approximately $ 16,600 and there are no minimum payments required.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing establishes a $15.265m contingent-payment liability while the supplied bridge shows no corresponding deduction. Even deducting the entire recorded liability would reduce values only to approximately $16.02, $20.81 and $24.36 per share, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged relative to the $43.68 price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that forecast OE does not already include settlement payments, then deduct the latest fair-value liability—or a better filed expected-payment estimate—from equity value in the next rerun.

audit_findings.title: A one-time acquisition hedge gain may remain in latest-year owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.252m pretax; the filing's pro forma after-tax adjustment was $7.058m
audit_findings.mechanism: If not purged, the acquisition-specific derivative gain increases FY2025 net income and recurring OE without representing ongoing operating earning power.
audit_findings.evidence: The settlement resulted in a gain of $ 9,252 , which was recorded as gain on derivative in the Company's Consolidated Statements of Operations for the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not demonstrate whether the gain was removed from the $105.4m anchor. However, even the conservative mechanical removal of the full $9.252m pretax amount would reduce scenario values only to approximately $14.91, $19.28 and $22.52 per share, all still far below the $43.68 market price. The possible error therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion on its own.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2025 OE reconciliation for a derivative-gain purge and, if absent, remove the filed $7.058m after-tax effect while treating related acquisition hedge losses or costs consistently.

audit_findings.title: Gross bridge cash may not all belong to or be distributable to parent common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $94.739m total bridge cash, including $78.618m held at foreign subsidiaries; constrained portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: NCI-owned, restricted, operationally required or tax-burdened cash would reduce the cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Of the total cash and cash equivalents, as of December 31, 2025, $93,859, or approximately 83%, was held in our foreign subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The distributable portion is unresolved, but the issue is bounded by the entire $94.739m bridge balance. Removing all bridge cash would reduce every scenario by approximately $1.26 per share, producing values of about $14.96, $19.75 and $23.30 per share—still well below the $43.68 price. Thus even the extreme case does not change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain subsidiary-level cash, ownership, restriction, covenant, operating-cash and repatriation-tax schedules; replace gross cash with verified excess parent-attributable cash in the next bridge.
